newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Western Australia focuses on union ballot law.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Western Australia focuses on union ballot law.

text.p: Western Australian Resources Development Minister, who is also leader of government business, said legislation to make unions hold secret ballots before calling a strike would be the goverment's main priority in the autumn session of the Western Australian parliament.

The autumn session is the first since the December 14 state election, which saw the Liberal-National party coalition returned with an increased majority of three seats in the lower house, the Legislative Assembly.

However, the coalition faces a hung upper house after losing its one-seat majority in the legislative council, although the term of the current council members will not expire until May 21 because members of this house are elected for a fixed four-year term.
Secret ballots were on the government's legislative agenda in 1994 but were dropped in the face of threatened industrial action from the trades union movement.

A spokesman for industrial relations Minister Graham Kierath said new industrial relations legislation will also require unions to disclose political donations and prohibit their access to non-union worker records.
"The minister (Kierath) is confident the industrial relations legislation will be given an early priority," the spokesman said.
State governor Major-General Michael Jeffery was to outline the government's full legislative programme when he formally opens parliament at 2.30 p.m. (0630 GMT) on Thursday.
